doc.title: Jane Jarvis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Orphaned and sent to Chicago on conservatory scholarships
summary: After her parents were killed by a train she was sent to Chicago, with scholarships at Bush Conservatory and DePaul.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, my parents were killed by a train. And so some terrible tragedy like that you know really brings out the kindness in people. And so a lot of people became interested in me that probably would have said oh isn’t that too bad and that would be the end of it. But I was sent in to Chicago to get instruction and wound up, I always got scholarships. And I got my first scholarship, it was a Bush Conservatory, which then became Chicago Conservatory, which then became the music school for Loyola University. And I also had a scholarship at DePaul University. And this was, there was so much attention you see, my mother being in the school system, in the public school system, it was general knowledge about this youngster, and I had no brothers or sisters. It was just like a novel. In fact my whole life is like a novel.
I see a book there, don’t you?
Well, come to think of it— Okay, now did I answer the question there?
You started, you had some more formal education.
